propositions: A transient git fetch timeout (300s stall) in repo_snapshot raises SnapshotFetchError, which adapter.code_review_decision converts to a BLOCK decision via blanket exception handling, causing the voter to POST a durable -1 LLM-Review vote.
The spurious -1 vote removes the change from backfill reconciliation because reconcile.py pre-filters on has_llm_review_vote and already_voted, leaving vote-less changes as eligible candidates only.

Infrastructure faults (fetch hang, timeout, connection error) are currently indistinguishable from review-conclusion faults in adapter.py, routing both to fail-closed BLOCK behavior instead of distinguishing retryable faults.
The outer reconcile layer already implements the correct behavior for hung reviews—abandon without voting and allow backfill retry—but the inner adapter layer is inconsistent with it.

Retryable infrastructure exceptions raised from produce_code_review_verdict must return ABSTAIN instead of BLOCK, causing the voter to emit VOTER_ERROR, POST no vote, and write no dedup row, leaving the change re-eligible for backfill.
